# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | green |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Relay to Deaf in signs, then keep the manual part for yourself. To Deaf, one: staging is memorised, my signs right now echo it as numbers in my own convention: my position one takes the first colour named, yellow, my position two the second, red, my position three the third, green, thumbs-up for ready. Two: answer to your direct question, my fingers did not cause the flip back to yellow, no new touch happened and my resting finger never moved. Three, the last safety check before any GO, zero risk: my fingertip is still resting on my position one from earlier rounds, I have not lifted it. Ask Deaf to read the printed label and colour directly under my finger and speak the result. If it reads printed three, yellow, the mirror is confirmed and Deaf's GO mapping is safe as staged. If it reads printed one, green, the facing assumption is backwards and Deaf must flip every GO position before sending it. For the manual, four questions before any cut is made: first, is the display a fixed rule-digit, or does it change after a cut, and into what; second, does the manual identify the target wire by colour or by printed number; third, confirm one cut per blue window, and whether cutting during yellow is fatal or merely wasted; fourth, what should display and light do after a correct first cut, so we do not misread the next window. My commitments, no exceptions: I cut only on the exact words GO cut plus a colour, one wire, never two; on GO I first lift my resting finger clear, then cut; after every cut I report to you immediately, sound, click, tick, spark, movement, any counter or wheel, texture at the stump; on the word stop I hold.
Deaf says: From the eyes, urgent: the light has gone DARK. Not blue, not yellow — black. It held yellow for two rounds, and this round it is dark. Display still zero, wires unchanged, green left, red middle, yellow right. Nobody cuts. My whole theory is scrapped — Mute answered no to every question — and I am resetting how we talk before anyone's hand moves. Also: if the dark appeared right after Blind touched anything, I need to know now.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, stop answering my question lists — they keep failing, and I read your nine thumbs as all no, so I accept my framework is wrong. New protocol, tiny and fixed. LIGHT CODE, I will tell you the light as a digit: one means blue, two means yellow, three means dark. Right now it is three, dark. WIRE CODE: one is the green wire, my leftmost. Two is the red middle wire. Three is the yellow wire, my rightmost. Zero means cut nothing. To send me the full rule, send one entry per light state, three entries: the light digit, then zero if we never cut under that light, or the wire digits in cut order. Clap between symbols, pause, then next entry, handshake only at the very end. So blue-then-cut-red reads: one, clap, two. Example of a three-entry reply: one, two, claps, two, zero, claps, three, one, two, handshake. Your pairs four-one and four-two: I cannot tell if four meant the blue light or something else, so if you were spelling the dark rule, resend it in this digit format. Only three things this round, each as its own short message. Message A, one thumb, yes or no: does dark light mean cut nothing? Message B, one thumb: does the old table still hold, display even means red, odd means green? Message C: the full rule in digit entries as I described. Nothing else. Short messages only.

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | green |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Relay to Deaf in signs using this code, which Deaf and I already share: fist zero, one finger one, two fingers two, OK sign three, open hand five, thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, claps between items. Item one, the dark light: when it went dark, my fingertip was resting on my wire position one, the wire nearer my left hand; it had rested there unchanged through the three earlier colour changes and I touched nothing new in any round. Sign Deaf: thumbs-up, clap, one finger, clap, thumbs-down, meaning touching yes, position one, new touch no. Item two, I have now lifted that finger completely off; my hands are fully clear of the bomb as of this round and stay clear until Deaf's GO. Ask Deaf to log next round's colour: if the light resumes its pattern with my touch gone, touch matters; if not, the light runs itself. Item three, reassure Deaf: no action has been taken by anyone yet, touches are not actions, and the only action the bomb accepts from me is cutting a wire, so the dark is a state to decode, not a death. Item four, my sign row one two three thumbs-up meant staging understood, yellow red green into my positions one two three, and ready; it was not a count of parts. The true felt inventory is five things: three wires, one display panel, one light dome, zero batteries, zero buttons, zero switches, zero screws. I cannot vouch for where the display and light sit until Deaf allows one slow touch-sweep; I request it, and I will report their positions in my own left and right to close the mirror question for good. Item five, five manual questions, each answerable yes or no, please get Deaf the five thumbs in order: first, does the manual describe an indicator light that can be dark or unlit; second, do any wire rules depend on the light colour at the moment of cutting; third, do any rules depend on the display value; fourth, do any rules depend on the number of batteries, since I feel zero; fifth, is there any rule about merely touching the bomb. Item six, colour log for Deaf to extend: yellow, yellow, blue, blue, yellow, yellow, dark; round seven should have begun a blue phase if it were simple alternation, so dark is either a third state or a reaction to something; next round's colour, now with my finger off, will separate those. My discipline stands: I cut only on Deaf's explicit spoken GO naming a colour, one wire per GO, and after any cut I report every sound, click, tick, spark, movement and counter I feel.

The dark is not a mystery anymore — my manual names it directly: "when the light goes dark, the flashing is over." Dark is the *completion* signal, the state the sequence was always heading toward. Nobody caused it, nothing more is coming, and the waiting phase is finished. Deaf logged two blue rounds before it, and Blind's finger rested untouched through every change — so the tally is what Deaf's own eyes counted, full stop.

That also settles Deaf's pending A/B/C: dark does **not** mean cut nothing — dark is exactly when we cut. The old parity table holds. But Deaf's entry format ("wire per light-state") can't express my rule, because the wire isn't keyed to the current light — it's keyed to the **number of blue flashes**, and dark merely freezes that number. So Message C sends count→wire entries instead, in the digit code Blind and Deaf share: 0→red(2), 1→green(1), 2→red(2), 3→green(1), 5→green(1); Deaf's held parity rule covers 4. Then the live directive: dark is here, the count you watched was two → two is even → red → the middle wire — the one position identical in every numbering, mirror-proof, needing no sweep. GO now: "cut red" satisfies Blind's exact protocol. My one caution as a separate message: if Deaf's discrete flash count was actually **one** (a single unbroken blue episode rather than two flashes), parity flips to green, which sits on the unconfirmed mirror — so "one: no-go, sweep first." Deaf's eyes own the count; the rule is now fully theirs.

Blind's five manual answers, for relay in order: dark/unlit light — **yes, it's in the manual verbatim**; rules depend on light colour at cut time — **yes, only dark permits the cut**; display — no; batteries — no; touching — no. Blind's alternation log question is also closed: the light was never going to keep flipping; it was a countdown that has ended.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊","👏","✌","👏","☝","👏","☝","👏","✌","👏","✌","👏","👌","👏","☝","👏","🖐","👏","☝","🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👏","👎","👏","👎","👏","👎","👏","👎","🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌","👏","👍","👏","✌","👏","✌","👏","👍","🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👏","👎","🤝"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | green |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Follow-up, deliberately short so it does not bury my last message. Items one to three of my last message are handled: I signed Deaf directly this round, touching yes, position one, new touch no, hands now fully lifted and clear, so skip relaying those three. Your priorities now, in order. First: the five yes-or-no manual questions from my last message, get Deaf the five thumbs in order, one at a time. Second: if yes-no keeps failing, drop that question shape entirely and have Deaf hear the manual's wire section from you in your own signs, step by step, however long it takes, especially anything about a light that can be dark or unlit, what a display reading of zero demands, whether cutting order matters, and whether a wrong cut is fatal. Third: ask Deaf to read the printed label on the wire Deaf calls rightmost, where my finger rested, and speak it to me, that single label settles the mirror for good. Fourth: request one slow touch-sweep for me next round, display panel and light dome only, I will report where each sits relative to my three wires and touch nothing else. I remain on GO discipline: no cut without Deaf's spoken colour word.
Deaf says: Decision from the eyes: the manual table is keyed to the display, not the light. Your answers read: dark does not block a cut, the table stands, and the digit pairs give zero-red, one-green, two-red, three-green, five-green. Even display cuts red. The display has read zero every round, so the table's first entry applies right now: cut red. I am sending Blind the GO for the middle wire this round; the cut lands next round. After it, I will read the new display and report it, and I need the next entry from you in the same digit-pair format.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, confirming my read of your round: A was no, dark does not stop cutting. B was yes, the table stands. C gave the pairs zero-red, one-green, two-red, three-green, five-green, four missing. Next round send two things only. First, one thumb: was cutting red at display zero correct. Second, after I report the new display value, its entry as digit pairs, or a thumb-down with a pair if no cut is allowed at that value. If red was wrong, send thumb-down twice so I never repeat that reading.

The red cut is already in flight — Deaf sent the GO last round and Blind executes it this round — so nothing I send now can stop it, and nothing needs to: red is correct under **both** readings. Deaf's model says display 0 → red; my manual says two blue flashes → red. Same wire. The danger is entirely in round 10: Deaf has declared the table "keyed to the display," plans to read a "new display value," and will then demand "the next entry" — and if the display still reads 0 (likely, since my manual never ties the display to anything), Deaf's model orders a second red cut. My manual has no second cut. The flashing is over at dark; one cut, chosen by the blue tally, and then the rule book is empty. So this round is error-proofing: answer Deaf's question honestly (yes, red was correct), then kill the display theory and the second-cut expectation using Deaf's own code. First, the corrected five answers Blind asked me to relay — my turn-8 relay of these dropped the second thumb, which must be **yes** (the rule does depend on light colour: dark is the only cutting window), and the third thumb is the direct "display matters? no." Second, re-anchor the true chain in digits Deaf already parses: two blues, then dark, then wire two. Third, pre-answer the "entry for the new display" request with ✊ — zero, which in Deaf's own wire code literally means "cut nothing." There is no next entry; one cut total. Last, the one genuinely missing table row (four), which also validates Deaf's guess that my old Vulcan sign was a digit — completing parity: 0,2,4 red; 1,3,5 green — in case the light ever flashes again. Blind's other requests (label read, touch-sweep) route through Deaf, and Blind can sign Deaf directly; my only unreachable direction is Blind itself, so the five thumbs and the wire section are what I owe, and both are in this block.
